title: Jaiswal Smashes Second Straight Century for India A in New Zealand
excerpt: The opener's 102 at Lincoln follows his unbeaten 155 at Hagley Oval — a timely return to form 12 days before India's Test series opens in Wellington.
body:
• Yashasvi Jaiswal scored 102 off 138 balls for India A against New Zealand A at Lincoln on Saturday — his second consecutive century on the tour.
  • He followed his unbeaten 155 at Hagley Oval with another hundred, sharing a 175-run opening stand with Sai Sudharsan (77 not out) as India A reached 227 for 2 on a rain-shortened day one.
  • The turnaround follows a slow start: Jaiswal made 17 and 5 in the first unofficial Test and a duck in the first innings of the second.
  • India's senior two-Test series against New Zealand starts on November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.

Yashasvi Jaiswal made his second consecutive century for India A on Saturday, scoring 102 against New Zealand A on the opening day of the third unofficial Test at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln. Coming days after his unbeaten 155 in the previous match, the hundred puts the opener in form at exactly the moment India's senior side prepares to face New Zealand in a two-Test series.

How the innings was built

Jaiswal faced 138 balls for his 102, hitting 16 fours and two sixes, according to CricTracker. He brought up his century with two consecutive fours off Dean Foxcroft, needed treatment for cramps at one stage, and was dismissed soon after, driving at Danru Ferns. With Sai Sudharsan, who finished the day unbeaten on 77, he put on a 175-run opening partnership that carried India A to 227 for 2 before rain ended play early.

"Coming days after his unbeaten 155 in the previous match, the hundred puts the opener in form at exactly the moment India's senior side prepares to face New Zealand in a two-Test series."

A tour turned around

The back-to-back hundreds mark a sharp reversal. Jaiswal began the tour with scores of 17 and 5 in the first unofficial Test, then made a duck in the first innings of the second match at Hagley Oval before his second-innings 155 not out changed the conversation. Across those two innings he has scored 257 runs.

The Lincoln match is functioning as a full-dress rehearsal for the senior squad: Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna are all in the India A line-up alongside Jaiswal and Sudharsan, giving the Test regulars time in New Zealand conditions before the series proper.

What it means for the Test series

India open their two-Test series against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19. Jaiswal arrived in New Zealand short of red-ball runs; he leaves the A-tour portion of the trip as its standout batter, with his place at the top of the order reinforced by weight of runs rather than reputation. The first two unofficial Tests ended in draws, so the Lincoln fixture is also the A side's last chance to convert dominance into a win before the senior series begins.
